resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Construction / Code Enforcement Office (Housing and Zoning Officer)
requirements: Handrails on stairs with 3 or more risers; guardrails on porches or decks 30 inches or higher
No broken windows or doors; all must work
Switch plates and outlet covers in place; light fixtures with shades and no bare wires
No holes in walls or other structural damage; no exterior damage or roof leaks
Smoke detector on every level, within 10 feet of bedroom doors and in every bedroom
Carbon monoxide detector in the hallway within 10 feet of bedroom doors
Mounted ABC fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (2017 list)
Breaker panel wired with no missing breakers
Hot and cold running water, working toilet, working heater; water heater relief valve extension 2 to 6 inches from the floor
4-inch white post 3 feet tall by the driveway with 3-inch reflective house numbers on two sides
No trash, motor vehicles or debris in the yard; all utilities on at the time of inspection
Bathroom window or exhaust fan; GFCI outlets within 3 feet of sinks
No flaking paint or stains on interior finishes; no double-keyed deadbolts
Water certificate from the Cumberland County Health Department and a septic certification

resale_co.notes: Township Code 175-13 (Ord. 93-330, amended 2001) requires the owner, on any transfer of title or change in occupancy of a residential unit, to get a certification from the Township Construction Official or Housing/Zoning Official that the unit has the required smoke detectors and meets the Property Maintenance Code; a transfer without it can be fined up to $500 (175-14). The live site (https://www.commercialtwp.com/) shows a bot check, and the Internet Archive could not be reached on this check, so the archive copies used last time (old Housing page captured 2025-03-21, CCO form 'Updated: March 20, 2017', Construction page captured 2025-06-14, Contact Us captured 2026-04-01) were not re-opened; their quotes are kept from the last check. Those pages list a $75 resale CCO fee and $40 re-inspection. The Township Code fee schedule for the Uniform Construction Code (131-3C(6), last amended 2020) lists 'Continued certificate of occupancy: Residential: $168', which does not match the $75 on the Township form; confirm which applies. The code was read in full through the ecode360 print view. No email is published for the Construction Office. Rental units must be registered and inspected every year (Chapter 258); that is a rental program.

requirements: The Township's CCO checklist (2017) checks smoke detectors on every level, within 10 feet of bedroom doors and in every bedroom, a CO detector within 10 feet of bedroom doors, and a mounted ABC fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA (registry code S) is the fire code enforcing agency for Commercial Township, but the DCA's July 17, 2026 state towns list shows Commercial without the 'SC' (smoke certs) flag and the DCA fire district data feed marks COMMERCIAL TWP-001 as smoke-certificate exempt, so the DCA online certificate is not offered here. Township Code 175-13 fills the gap: on a transfer of title the owner gets the smoke detector certification from the Township Construction Official or Housing/Zoning Official, which is done with the Township's resale CCO inspection. No separate smoke certificate fee is published. The state fire directory lists Louis Kilmer (NJ DCA Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement, (609)633-6132; the Bureau's page gives (609) 633-6106) as the fire official for Commercial. The 2017 CCO list still requires a fire extinguisher; the February 3, 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed it from the state requirement. Township Code 175-13 mentions only smoke detectors; CO alarms are checked on the CCO list.
